summary: Not on these pairs. On BTC, ETH and SOL, every Stochastic setting on 1h and 4h did the same as random entries, whether it bought below 20 or shorted above 80. Same as random on 1h and 4h. On daily, price kept rising after readings above 80, but only because of signals between Jul 29 and Sep 9, 2021. Without them it was the same as random.

notes: On 1h, the default timeframe, %K crossing up %D below 20 gave 3,102 entries in 1,673 separate moves. Twenty candles later they matched random entries, inside a luck band of -0.16% to 0.22%. %K below 20 enters about eight times as often and lands at 0.03%, also inside the band. BTC, ETH and SOL each came out the same as random on both settings.

On daily, %K crossing up through 20 gave 401 entries in 122 moves. Twenty days later they were 3.81% worse than random. That holds without its strongest stretch, between Apr 13 and Jul 13, 2022, and at 50 candles, but not at 10 or 100. Neither trend carries it alone: in uptrends it rests on signals between Nov 19, 2021 and Jan 11, 2022, in downtrends it was the same as random, and on 1h and 4h the same cross was the same as random.

On daily, shorting after %K crossed down %D above 80 did 4.69% worse than random after 20 days, and %K above 80 did 3.78% worse. Both rest on one stretch, between Aug 1 and Sep 9, 2021 for the cross and between Jul 29 and Sep 9, 2021 for the level, and are the same as random without it. SOL carried it: on SOL alone the cross did 12% worse than random, while BTC and ETH were the same as random. The result sits in uptrends only. In downtrends both settings were the same as random.

On 4h, both shorts above 80 were the same as random pooled, but in uptrends they were not. There, %K crossing down %D above 80 did 0.61% worse than random and %K above 80 did 0.38% worse. Each rests on one stretch, between Aug 11 and Aug 17, 2021 and between Aug 4 and Sep 9, 2021, and is the same as random without it. In downtrends both were the same as random. On 1h, %K below 20 beat random by 0.08% in downtrends, but that rests on 10 entries on Jul 16, 2022 and shows at 20 candles only.

One pair-level result holds. On ETH 4h, %K crossing up %D below 20 did 1.43% worse than random after 20 candles. It holds without its strongest stretch, Jun 11–13, 2022, around the Celsius withdrawal freeze, and at 10 candles, but not at 50 or 100. On BTC and SOL, and pooled, the same setting was the same as random.

For a long DCA bot on 1h or 4h, Stochastic below 20 or crossing up from below 20 added nothing over random timing on these pairs. The DCA orders and take profit do the work, and leaving the condition out costs nothing that this data can measure. On daily, the cross up through 20 is a reason to leave that setting out of a long bot's start conditions. For a short bot, readings above 80 were followed by further gains in uptrends, so a filter that keeps it off while the pair is above its 200-day SMA removes those deals. Test that filter on your own pair.
